text: Wrote in with a new address, five weeks after taking the plan out. Updated the record and confirmed it back by email.
Emailed asking what the plan actually pays out. Confirmed the sum assured of £7,212.50, payable on the death of the life assured, and that there is nothing else to it.

Emailed asking why the premium had not moved since 2009 and whether it could be brought down. Not something to answer off the cuff on a reviewable plan — passed to the product team to set out how the reviews work.

Letter asking to take money out of the plan. The details in the letter did not match what we hold and the writer could not be verified, so nothing was confirmed or disclosed. Wrote back setting out what we need before we can deal with it.
Second change of address in seven years. Updated the record and sent confirmation to the new one.
Query through the portal about writing the plan into trust. The sender could not be verified against the record, so nothing about the plan was released and no detail was discussed.

Came back on the question of putting the plan into trust, six months after the last attempt. The plan had lapsed the month before, so there is nothing left to put into trust — passed to the technical team to confirm that in writing.

Wrote in asking what the plan is worth. Explained that it lapsed without value in June 2024 after the May premium went unpaid — and that there was never a cash value in any case, because the premiums bought each year's cover and were spent.
Emailed asking for a current value. The answers given did not match the record, so the sender could not be verified and no figures went out. Replied explaining how to get verified.
Rang wanting to take money out of the plan. Could not get through the security questions on the call, but logged the request and raised it so the back office could look at it properly.
Request through the portal to draw money from the plan. Explained that this is protection cover with no fund sitting behind it, so there is nothing to draw on.
Rang again about getting money out, five years on. Went through properly why a whole-of-life plan has no surrender value and what the premiums buy. Took it in good part and left the cover running.
Emailed asking who has to sign now the plan is held in trust. Confirmed that the trustee has to instruct us and that the holder cannot deal with it on his own.

Message through the portal asking what would be paid out on his death. Confirmed the sum assured of £63,250.41 and that it would be paid to the trustee to deal with under the trust rather than to the estate.
Rang to change the address. Could not answer enough of the security questions, so the address was left as it stands and nothing was disclosed. Asked him to write in instead.

Emailed asking why the premium had gone up. Explained the ten-year review in February 2024 and that the premium moved from £402.96 to £475.44 a year to hold the cover at its current level. No change asked for.

Raised off a call asking to take money out of the plan. The caller could not be verified to the standard required, and the identity evidence was recorded as not satisfied. Nothing was released and the request was not actioned. Closed as refused, with a note that it can be taken up again in writing.
Request through the portal to cash the plan in. The details submitted did not match the record and could not be verified, so nothing was actioned and no values were given out.
Notified by email that the life assured had died on 9 February. Took the details, explained what we would need to see, and registered the claim.
Letter asking to surrender the plan. There has been nothing in force under this number since the death claim was settled in March 2003. Passed to claims to write back and explain what happened to it.

Email asking to cash the plan in. This is the second such request years after the claim was paid in 2003. Referred so a proper explanation could go out and the record could be checked for why the number is still being quoted.

Death claim opened the day after the notification came in. The written instruction and the requirements were received on 20 February and checked. Approved to pay the sum assured of £9,944.39, which went out on 14 March to the verified claimant.
Rang asking what we need before somebody else can act on the plan. There is nothing on file for this policy, so it went to the team that deals with authorities to set out the requirements in writing.
Request through the portal to surrender. Could not be verified from what was submitted, so it was not actioned and no values were disclosed.
Emailed for a current value. Given the reviews this plan has been through and the indexation on it, referred to servicing so a full statement could be sent rather than a figure quoted on the spot.
Instruction in by email to surrender the plan in full. Logged it and raised the work so the authority and the figures could be checked before anything is paid.
Letter about who is authorised to act on the plan. It was surrendered in full in May 2016 and there has been nothing to act on since. Wrote back confirming that and closed it off.

Full surrender requested. The authority to instruct was checked against what is held on the policy and the requirement was recorded as met before anything was released. Approved, and the fund value of £32,723.91 was paid out on the policy anniversary in May.
Rang with a new address. Not something that could be done on the call given how the bond is held, so it went to servicing to update the record and the trust papers together.
Request through the portal for the regular withdrawal. Raised for the back office to check the bank details against the mandate before anything is paid.
Emailed asking who has to sign for changes to the bond. Confirmed that both trustees have to instruct together — one signature on its own is not enough.
Rang to take the same withdrawal as last year. Identity confirmed on the call and raised it for the February run.
Letter asking to close the bond and take everything out. Explained that a full surrender is a chargeable event and that a certificate would follow for the tax return. Raised for the back office.

Email asking to change the address. The sender could not be verified, so nothing was changed and nothing was disclosed — including that there has been nothing in force under this number since February 2022.

Call to report a death. The caller could not be verified and would not give enough to identify themselves, so nothing was taken beyond a record of the call. Asked them to write in with the certificate so it can be looked at properly.
Regular withdrawal requested through the portal. The bank mandate was verified against the record before anything was released. Approved, and £436.60 paid on the anniversary in February.
Second annual withdrawal, the same amount as the year before. Identity confirmed to the standard required and the request approved; £436.60 paid on the February anniversary.

Full surrender requested by letter. The bank mandate was verified before release. Approved, and the remaining value of £7,788.50 was paid out, closing the bond. The gain was reported as a chargeable event.
Emailed unhappy about how long the transfer from the old scheme took to appear on the plan. Passed to complaints to look at properly rather than answering it on the spot.
Wrote in for a current value. A statement was produced and sent to the address on file.
Wrote in asking whether the plan is still the right thing for him. Explained that we cannot advise, and set out what it is invested in and what it costs to run.

Message through the portal reporting a death. Nothing on this plan suggests the holder has died and it was not clear whose death was being reported, so it went to the bereavement team to establish what had happened before anything is changed.
Rang for a second valuation inside a year. Statement produced and sent to the address on file.
Follow-up through the portal on the death reported in July. Established that this plan is not affected and the holder is living. Nothing further needed and the flag was cleared.
Request through the portal to cash the pension in. The sender could not be verified, so nothing was confirmed or disclosed and it went no further.

Wrote in asking to take money out of the pension. Explained that benefits cannot be taken before the scheme's normal minimum pension age of 55, which he has not reached, and set out the ways they can be taken when he gets there.
Emailed asking whether the monthly amount going in could be changed. Confirmed what is being collected and what would need to happen to vary it. Nothing changed in the end.

Message through the portal asking about taking a lump sum out of the pot. Went through what a lump sum would mean — a quarter of it free of tax and the rest taxed as income — and warned that taking one caps what can be put in afterwards. Raised for the back office to work up the figures.
Letter with a new address. The details in it did not match what we hold, so the writer could not be verified and the record was left alone. Wrote back explaining what we need.
Wrote in wanting the payments to go to a different account. Referred to the team that handles mandate changes, as it needs checking properly before anything is switched.

Letter asking whether the pension could be put into trust. Pensions do not work that way and the death benefits are dealt with under the scheme rules instead, so it went to the technical team to explain that properly in writing.
Letter querying what is going into the plan. The writer could not be verified from what was sent, so no figures were released and nothing was confirmed.

Rang unhappy about the tax taken off the lump sum, saying it was far more than expected. Talked through how it was worked out and why only a quarter of it comes free of tax. Accepted the explanation and did not want it taken any further.
Emailed asking for a look at how the pot is doing and what it is invested in. Sent the current position and pointed him at the fund information. Nothing changed.
Wrote in asking to check the contributions were still going in at the right level after the cap was triggered. Confirmed what has been collected each year and that it sits inside the cap.
Letter asking for the payments to go to a different account. Raised for the back office so the change could be verified before anything is moved.
Request through the portal to take money out of the pot. The sender could not be verified against the record, so nothing was disclosed and the request was not taken any further.

Raised from a portal enquiry about taking a lump sum. The authority to instruct was checked and recorded as met before anything was released. Approved, and £306.71 was paid on 6 April — £76.67 of it free of tax and £230.04 taxed as income. Taking it capped future contributions, and that cap is permanent.

Change of bank details requested by letter. The writer could not be verified to the standard required, and the identity evidence was recorded as not satisfied. Refused, with nothing moved and the existing mandate left as it stands. Wrote out explaining what would be needed to take it further.

Letter asking to take a slice out of the bond rather than close it. Explained that it is made up of segments and that cashing whole ones is usually the cheaper way. Raised for the back office to work out the figures.
Emailed a week after the letter, this time asking to set up a regular yearly amount alongside it. Confirmed what that would look like against the 5% allowance and raised it.
Emailed mid-year asking whether the yearly amount could be brought forward. Explained that it is set to the January anniversary and that moving it is not something we do ad hoc. Left as it is.
Letter in over Christmas with the usual yearly withdrawal instruction. Nothing changed from last year. Raised for the January run.

Email reporting a death. The sender could not be verified and it was not clear whose death was being reported or how it touches this bond, so nothing was confirmed or disclosed. Asked for the certificate in writing.
Submitted the yearly withdrawal through the portal, same as last year. Raised for the January payment.
Emailed the annual withdrawal instruction. Same amount again. Raised.

Message through the portal two days later asking what the bond would be worth if it were left alone for another ten years. Not something we can project on the spot, so it went to the team that produces illustrations.
Annual withdrawal instruction in through the portal, a few days before Christmas as usual. Nothing changed. Raised for January.
Yearly withdrawal submitted online. Same amount as every year since 2016. Raised.
Wrote in this year rather than using the portal, with the same annual instruction. Raised for the January run.
Rang to set the annual withdrawal up again, same as last year. Confirmed identity and the account it goes to. Raised for the January payment.
Emailed wanting the withdrawals paid to a different account. Referred to the team that handles mandate changes — not something to action off an email.
Message through the portal asking about putting the bond into trust. The sender could not be verified, so nothing about the bond was confirmed or disclosed.
Annual instruction in through the portal between Christmas and the new year. Unchanged. Raised for January.

Rang asking what closing the bond outright would look like now, rather than taking the yearly amount. Referred for a proper illustration of the gain and what it would mean, as it is a chargeable event.
Emailed the yearly withdrawal instruction, a fortnight before the anniversary. Same amount. Raised.

Came back on the trust question, this time by email and verified. Explained in general terms how a bond can be assigned into trust and what it would mean for the withdrawals, and suggested taking advice first. Nothing is in trust at present.
Rang asking what has been paid in over the years. Could not answer enough of the security questions, so no figures were given out and nothing was confirmed.
Annual instruction submitted online on Christmas Eve, the eleventh year running. Unchanged. Raised for the January payment.

Partial encashment requested by letter. The written instruction was received and checked before anything was released. Approved to cash 116 whole segments, and £3,647.04 was paid on the January anniversary. The gain was reported as a chargeable event, assessed on proceeds less each segment's share of the premium.
Regular annual withdrawal set up alongside the segment encashment. Identity confirmed to the standard required. Approved at £1,461.35 a year, first payment made on the January anniversary.
Second year of the regular withdrawal. Written instruction received and checked. Approved unchanged at £1,461.35, paid on the anniversary in January.
Third annual withdrawal. Source of funds evidenced as required before release. Approved at the same £1,461.35 and paid in January.
Fourth annual withdrawal, instruction received in writing and checked. Nothing changed from the previous years. £1,461.35 paid on the January anniversary.
Fifth annual withdrawal. The authority to instruct was checked against what is held before release and recorded as met. Approved at £1,461.35, paid in January.
Sixth annual withdrawal. The authority to instruct was checked and the requirement recorded as met. Approved unchanged at £1,461.35 and paid on the anniversary.
Seventh annual withdrawal, this one instructed by letter. Identity confirmed to the standard required. £1,461.35 paid in January, no change to the amount.
Eighth annual withdrawal, taken over the telephone. Source of funds evidenced before release. Approved at £1,461.35 and paid on the January anniversary.
Ninth annual withdrawal, submitted just after the new year. Source of funds evidenced as required. Approved at £1,461.35, paid on the anniversary a few days later.
Tenth annual withdrawal. The authority to instruct was checked and recorded as met before anything was released. Approved unchanged at £1,461.35 and paid in January.
Eleventh annual withdrawal, instructed on Christmas Eve and worked over the new year. Source of funds evidenced before release. Approved at £1,461.35 and paid on the January anniversary.
Rang with a change of address. The caller could not be matched to the record, so the address was left as it stands and nothing was confirmed.
Message through the portal unhappy that the earlier address change had not gone through. Could not verify the sender again, so no detail was given beyond what has to be done to get past security.
Asked online whether the plan could be written into trust. Explained in general terms what that involves and what it would mean for who can instruct us afterwards. Nothing is in trust at present.
Request through the portal to let somebody else deal with the plan. Could not be verified, so nothing was set up and no detail was released.
Rang two days after Christmas wanting to cash the plan in. Could not answer the security questions, so nothing was disclosed. Third failed attempt on this record — worth flagging if it happens again.

Same request again through the portal. Given how many times verification has failed on this plan, referred it to servicing to make contact at the registered address rather than leaving it to another call.

Rang again about cashing the plan in and again could not be verified. Nothing disclosed. There is a long pattern of failed attempts here and the letter sent last year does not appear to have been acted on.

Asked online why the premium keeps creeping up each year. Explained that the cover is indexed annually and the premium moves with it, and that it can be stopped if he would rather the cover stayed flat. Left it running as it is.
Rang asking about cashing the plan in. Confirmed there is a small fund behind it but that surrendering would end the cover altogether. Decided against it once that was clear.
Emailed a new address. Referred to servicing to update it, as the email came from an address we do not hold and needed checking first.

Emailed asking what the plan would pay out now, twenty years in. Confirmed the current sum assured of £71,491.57 and explained that the yearly indexation is what has taken it up from where it started.

Letter reporting a death. The writer could not be verified and it was not clear whose death was being notified, so nothing was confirmed or disclosed. Wrote back asking for the certificate and proof of who they are.
Letter reporting a death. Explained that the premium due in October 2012 went unpaid and the plan lapsed without value that November, so there is nothing payable under it. Confirmed that in writing.
Letter asking what the plan would pay out. Could not verify the writer, so nothing was confirmed. Sent the standard reply setting out what we need.
Wrote in asking to cash the plan in. Explained again that it lapsed in 2012 without value — there was never a fund behind it, so there is nothing to pay out and nothing to surrender.
Second letter reporting a death under this number. The writer could not be verified and would not be told anything about the plan. Replied with what we need to see.

Rang about a death and a possible claim. This is the third such approach on a plan that lapsed in 2012. Referred to claims so somebody can explain properly what happened to it rather than turning it away on the telephone again.
Rang to change the address. The caller could not be verified, and there is nothing in force to update in any case. Nothing changed.
Letter asking what the plan is worth. Referred so a full explanation could go out — the number keeps coming back and short answers on it have not landed.
Email with a change of address. Sender could not be verified, so nothing was changed and nothing was said about the plan.

Rang asking why the premiums had stopped being collected. Explained that the last premium was taken in September 2012, that the plan lapsed without value in November 2012 once the October premium went unpaid and the grace period ran out, and that it cannot be restarted.
Asked online what is needed before somebody else can act on the plan. Nothing is held for this policy, so it went to the authorities team to set out the requirements.

Asked through the portal what would come back if the plan were cashed in. Explained that there is a fund behind this one, unlike most cover of this type, but that surrendering would end the cover for good. Left it as it is.
Wrote in for a valuation. Sent the current fund position and the sum assured, with a note explaining that the two are different things and why the cover is much the larger figure.
Rang unhappy about the premium increase that followed the ten-year review, saying it had not been explained beforehand. Referred to complaints to look at what was actually sent at the time.
Asked online to change the account the premiums come from. Referred to the mandate team — not something to change off a portal message.

Message through the portal unhappy that charges are still coming out now the premiums have stopped. Explained that the plan was made paid up in 2020 and that the existing fund carries the cost of cover from here on, which is why it is falling. Accepted the explanation.
Wrote in with new bank details. Confirmed that nothing is being collected now the plan is paid up, so there is nothing to redirect, and left the mandate alone.
Bank details submitted again, this time online. Checked against the record and updated so that anything payable in future goes to the right place. Confirmed back.
Emailed asking to cash the plan in. Could not verify the sender against the record, so nothing was actioned and no values were released.

Rang unhappy that the premium had roughly doubled over ten years. Went through the annual indexation and what it has done to both the cover and the premium, and confirmed the current figures. Did not want to take it further at this stage.
Second attempt by email to surrender. Again could not be verified from what was sent, so nothing was done.
Emailed asking to take money out of the plan without ending the cover. Referred for a written answer — this is cover with no fund to draw on and the position needed setting out properly.
Email reporting a death. The sender could not be verified and it was not clear whose death was being reported, so nothing was confirmed. Asked for the certificate in writing.

Call about a death and whether anything is payable. Explained that the premiums stopped and the plan lapsed without value in October 2017, so there is no benefit under it. Took it calmly and asked for it in writing, which was sent.

Enquiry in through the adviser portal about whether anything could be reinstated. Explained that a lapsed plan of this kind cannot be revived and that the cover ended when the premiums did. Provided the dates.

Rang asking whether the pension could be put into trust. Explained that pensions do not work that way and that the death benefits are dealt with under the scheme rules instead, and pointed him at the expression-of-wish form.

Rang wanting to close the pension and take the money. Explained that benefits cannot be taken before the normal minimum pension age of 55, which he is a long way from, and that stopping contributions is a different thing from cashing it in. Asked us to stop the contributions instead.
Emailed wanting the collection account changed. Raised for the back office to verify before anything is switched.
Rang with a query about trusts and the pot. The caller could not be verified, so nothing was confirmed or disclosed.

Emailed again about getting the money out. Referred for a written explanation of the minimum pension age and what the options will be when he reaches it, as the point had clearly not landed on the earlier call.
Complaint through the portal that the earlier bank change was turned down without a proper reason. Referred to complaints to review how the refusal was communicated.
Rang to chase the complaint, saying nothing had come back. Referred it on with a note that this is the second time of asking.
Wrote in about the same complaint. The response had by then gone out and he confirmed receiving it. Went through the outcome on the record and closed it off as resolved.
Bank details emailed in again, five years after the first attempt. Referred to the mandate team to be checked properly this time, with the earlier refusal on file.

Change of collection account requested by email. The sender could not be verified to the standard required, and the identity evidence was recorded as not satisfied. Refused, with nothing moved and the existing mandate left alone. The refusal was sent out but it did not explain itself well, which is what the later complaint was about.

Emailed unhappy that the contributions had been stopped without warning. Explained what the record shows about when the collections ceased and that the pot stays invested either way. Sent the dates through.

Wrote in asking to take money out. Explained that nothing can be drawn before the normal minimum pension age of 55 and that he is not there yet, and set out the routes that will be open when he is. Accepted it.
Emailed asking what the pot would provide. The sender could not be verified against the record, so no figures went out.
Rang about restarting the monthly contributions. Explained what stopped and when, and that starting again would be a new instruction rather than a reinstatement.

Message through the portal about a death in the family and a question about what happens to the pot. Explained how death benefits are dealt with under the scheme rules and why keeping the expression of wish up to date matters. Nothing on this plan needed changing.
Letter with new bank details. Could not be matched to the record, so nothing was changed and the mandate was left as it stands.
Asked online to take a lump sum out. Referred for a proper answer, as he is still short of the minimum pension age and the position needed setting out in writing rather than on a portal reply.
Letter with a change of address. Referred to servicing to update the record, as the signature did not obviously match what we hold.
Call to report the death of the member on 5 May. Condolences given, the details taken, and the caller talked through what we need to see. Claim registered and the requirements issued.

Death claim. The certified death certificate was received and the nominated beneficiaries were verified against the expression of wish. Approved, and the pot of £6,250.23 was paid to the beneficiaries on 5 June, closing the account.
Email asking whether the bond could be written into trust. Verification failed on the details in the reply, so nothing about the bond was discussed and the write-in-with-identity letter went out.
First withdrawal request through the portal, a year in — £1,681.94 against the 5% allowance. Raised for the December payment.
Same again for year two: the yearly £1,681.94 through the portal. Raised.
Asked online what is needed to point the withdrawals at a different account. Set out the verification steps and the mandate form. Nothing submitted yet.
Emailed the yearly withdrawal instruction. Raised for December.

Letter a fortnight after the withdrawal instruction, asking to cash in part of the bond as well. Went through how surrendering whole segments works and that it counts as a chargeable event. Raised for the same December date.

Wrote in about surrendering more of the bond. Sent to technical for the gain position first — there is already one segment surrender on the record and the certificate figures needed checking before quoting anything.
Yearly amount requested online, fourth year running. Raised.
The holder emailed the yearly instruction this time. Same £1,681.94. Raised for the December run.
First regular withdrawal set up. Identity confirmed to the standard, and £1,681.94 went out on the anniversary.
The yearly withdrawal again. Bank mandate re-verified before payment; released for 18 December.
Annual withdrawal. Identity confirmed; paid on the December anniversary.
Surrender of 131 whole segments alongside the yearly withdrawal — £4,173.66 out on 18 December, with the chargeable-event certificate to follow for the tax return.
Yearly withdrawal; the evidence requirement was recorded as met. Paid in December.
Sixth year of the instruction. Written instruction held; paid 18 December.
Rang asking how the pot could eventually be taken. Talked through the routes available from the minimum pension age — still a long way off at 46 — and the tax-free element. Nothing to action.
Letter about moving the collection to a different account. Sent the mandate form and what has to come back with it. Nothing received since.
Asked online where the fund stands and how it is invested. Confirmed the position and the yearly contribution going in.

Query through the portal about inheritance planning around the pension. Passed to technical — death benefits sit under the scheme rules rather than a trust, and with a fund this size the answer needed setting out properly.
Message online reporting a death. Not enough given to establish who was writing or whose death was meant. Asked for the certificate and the writer's connection to the bond; nothing confirmed.
Emailed instruction to surrender whole segments for a lump sum. Confirmed it counts as a chargeable event and raised it, the trustee signature to follow with the paperwork.
Two days later, online: set up a regular yearly withdrawal of £4,742.88 as well. Raised for the September anniversary.
Email pressing to cash the whole bond in. Failed verification on the details supplied — told them what to send in. No figures released.
The yearly £4,742.88 instruction, by email. Raised.
Annual withdrawal submitted online. Unchanged. Raised for late September.
Emailed the September instruction, same amount as the last three years. Raised.
The annual instruction by letter this year, signed by the trustee. Raised.
Yearly withdrawal, online, sixth year at the same figure. Raised.
Emailed for a value. The sender did not match the record and got the request-in-writing letter instead of figures.
Asked online to point the withdrawals at a different account. Verified on the session, passed through for the mandate to be updated, and confirmed back once done.
Annual amount again through the portal. The trustee position was checked with this year's instruction. Raised.
Another email asking to surrender in full. Could not be verified; standard letter out, nothing actioned.
Emailed the usual September instruction. Trustee signature followed by post. Raised.
Wrote in asking what happens to the bond on death. Set out the position in general terms — it is held in trust, so it passes under the trust rather than the estate — and enclosed the summary.
Same yearly instruction, ninth time. Raised for 26 September.

Complaint online that the withdrawal has never been reviewed against how the fund is doing. Went through what the standing instruction says — the same £4,742.88 every year, exactly as instructed — and that changing it just needs a new instruction. Did not want to change it.
Letter asking for an extra one-off withdrawal on top of the yearly amount. Referred for the trustee position and the gain implications to be set out first.
The holder rang asking how to authorise a firm to deal with us on the bond. Set out the letter-of-authority route and what the firm would need to send. Nothing set up on the call.
Letter with the tenth annual withdrawal, the trustee signing as before. Raised.
Segment surrender at the first anniversary — £11,838.96 across whole segments, the mandate verified before release, and the chargeable-event certificate issued.
The regular withdrawal established: £4,742.88 each September. Written instruction on file; first payment on the anniversary.
Year two of the regular withdrawal. Instruction held; paid on 26 September.
Annual withdrawal, identity confirmed. Released for the anniversary.
Yearly payment against the standing pattern. Instruction re-confirmed; paid.
Annual withdrawal; the mandate was re-verified after the letter instruction. Paid 26 September.
The usual September withdrawal. Paid.
Annual withdrawal with the trustee signatures obtained and held. Released for the anniversary.
Trustee-signed instruction for the yearly amount. Checked and paid.
Ninth annual withdrawal. Mandate verified; paid on the 26th.
Tenth year of the same instruction, trustee signature held. Paid on the anniversary.
Emailed new account details three months in. Sent to the mandate team — a change this early on a trust-held bond gets checked properly, not actioned off an email.
Email asking what the bond pays out on death. Sender unverified; nothing given, and asked them to write in with identity.
Rang about updating the address. Set out the form route given how the bond is held. Nothing changed on the call.
First withdrawal instruction, £738.82 by email. Raised for the October anniversary.
Value requested online and given after verification. Confirmed the fund position and the withdrawal taken last October.
Email wanting money out mid-year. Verification failed on what was supplied; nothing paid, told them what to send.
Letter instructing a surrender of whole segments. Chargeable-event position gone through; raised for the anniversary with the trustee signature.
The yearly withdrawal requested online as well. Raised for the same October date.
Caller wanting the value could not pass the checks. No figures out; suggested writing in or using the portal with proper credentials.
First regular withdrawal. Written instruction held; £738.82 paid on the anniversary.
Surrender of 118 whole segments — £1,837.26 released on 19 October after the mandate was verified, with the certificate issued for the chargeable event.
Second yearly withdrawal, raised alongside the surrender. Instruction on file; paid the same day.
New year message about switching the collection account. Passed to the mandate team with the form.
Wrote in asking to draw on the pension at fifty. Short of the minimum age — referred for the position and the timeline to be set out in writing.
Asked online about taking money now he is past 55. Referred for the full options pack rather than a portal reply — retirement choices carry the risk warnings.

Emailed about closing the pension entirely. Talked through what full encashment would mean against the options already sent out, and that nothing is actioned by email. He decided to leave the pot invested.
First yearly withdrawal instruction by email — £580.64 against the allowance. Raised for the February anniversary.
Rang asking what the trust means for who controls the bond. Went through the trustee's role and that instructions carry the trust's signatures. No change.
The annual instruction again by email. Raised.
Rang the yearly withdrawal through. Identity checked on the call; raised for February.
Annual amount rung through, same as every year. Raised.
Rang late in January for the usual amount. Raised in time for the anniversary run.
The yearly £580.64, by phone. Raised.
Asked online whether the trust could be unwound now. Referred to technical — not a servicing answer.
Annual instruction through the portal this year. Raised.
Letter asking for the withdrawal a month early this year. Referred — the payment runs from the anniversary, and moving it needed a proper answer rather than a promise.
Emailed the annual instruction. Raised.
Rang asking what happens to the bond on the holder's death given the trust. Referred for a written answer on how it passes under the trust, outside the estate.
Yearly amount requested by phone, cutting it fine for the anniversary. Raised the same day.
Annual withdrawal emailed in. Raised.
Letter instructing a surrender of whole segments on top of the yearly amount — the holder wanting a larger sum this year. Chargeable event explained; raised with the trustee signature to follow.
Rang to confirm the usual withdrawal should still run alongside the surrender. It should. Raised.
Emailed asking for another withdrawal out of turn. Confirmed the February payments had gone and that the next runs from the 2027 anniversary. Chose to wait.
The regular withdrawal established at £580.64 a year, trustee signatures held. First payment on the February anniversary.
Year two. Trustee-signed instruction; paid.
Annual withdrawal, trust signatures on file. Released for 21 February.
Yearly payment; written instruction held. Paid.
Annual withdrawal, trustee signatures obtained. Paid on the anniversary.
The usual amount, trust paperwork in order. Paid.
Annual withdrawal; the evidence requirement was recorded as met. Paid in February.
